brief: Return from the outermost structured block
description: Return from the outermost structured block. If the expression of a lambda function is a block function, this will effectively return from the lambda function. Used as a value inside a larger expression, for example add(return(1), 2), it marks the block to return its value, but the rest of that statement is still evaluated first, side effects included; if that statement is itself a return, the later value replaces the earlier one. Outside a structured block, as in expression syntax, nothing is returned and the call evaluates to its value.

parameters.description: The value to evaluate that the outermost block will return. If not specified, the last evaluated value or a null value will be returned.
parameters.name: value

returns.description: This function returns from the outermost structured block with the last evaluated value.
